title: Conditional universal-arrow criterion for a coherent free module
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functors, mapping spaces and universes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and monoidal infinity-categories of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category]. Let $\mathcal V$ be a monoidal infinity-category and $\mathcal M$ an infinity-category with a coherent left action $\otimes:\mathcal V\times\mathcal M\to\mathcal M$: the equivalences $(v\otimes w)\otimes m\simeq v\otimes(w\otimes m)$ and $\mathbf1\otimes m\simeq m$ include all associative and unital higher compatibilities. An associative algebra $B$ in $\mathcal V$ has a multiplication $B\otimes B\to B$, a unit $\mathbf1\to B$ and their coherent compatibilities. A left $B$-module in $\mathcal M$ has an action $B\otimes m\to m$ with all coherent associativity and unit data; $\operatorname{LMod}_B(\mathcal M)$ retains the coherent action-preserving maps and their higher simplices. All categories and mapping spaces are taken in sufficiently large universes. Let $X\in\mathcal M$, let $L\in\operatorname{LMod}_B(\mathcal M)$ have action $b_L$, let $U$ forget the action, and let $\lambda:X\to UL$ be a morphism. Suppose the composite
$$B\otimes X\xrightarrow{B\otimes\lambda}B\otimes UL\xrightarrow{b_L}UL$$
is an equivalence. Then for every $N\in\operatorname{LMod}_B(\mathcal M)$ the map
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{LMod}_B(\mathcal M)}(L,N)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal M}(X,UN),\qquad f\longmapsto U(f)\lambda$$
is an equivalence of spaces, natural in $N$ and in coherent families of pairs $(L,\lambda)$. No existence of $L$ is asserted without the displayed hypothesis, and no colimit or presentability hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Higher Algebra, Definition 4.2.4.1 and Corollary 4.2.4.6, printed pp. 530-531 (the fixed-algebra consequence of Proposition 4.2.4.2(2)). Online 2017 source read; WANTED: archived Higher Algebra in literature/. No Stacks tag covers coherent infinity-categorical modules.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-module-operad-encoding] to the given action. Work over the base operad $\mathrm{LM}^\otimes$, with its cocartesian fibration $q:\mathcal E^\otimes\to\mathrm{LM}^\otimes$ and inclusion $i:\mathrm{LM}_0^\otimes\hookrightarrow\mathrm{LM}^\otimes$. The pair $(B,X)$ defines an $\mathrm{LM}_0$-algebra $A$, while $(B,L)$ defines an $\mathrm{LM}$-algebra $F$. Under the stated equivalence of algebra categories, $(\mathrm{id}_B,\lambda)$ is a coherent transformation $\eta:A\to i^*F$. This fixes the algebra coordinate rather than mistaking the whole category of LM-algebras for the category of modules over a fixed algebra.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.2.4.2: LM_0 and the equivalence with algebra-plus-object pairs.

proof.text: Compute the active slices $J_a$ and $J_m$ from [lem-coef-relative-operadic-terminal-active-mapping] using the operation lists in [lem-coef-module-operad-encoding]. An object of $J_a$ is an ordered list of $a$-inputs with its multiplication to $a$. It has a unique morphism to $\mathrm{id}_a$: multiply that list in $\mathrm{LM}_0$. Thus $\mathrm{id}_a$ is terminal. An object of $J_m$ is an ordered list of $r$ inputs of color $a$ followed by the single $m$-input, acting on $m$. It has a unique morphism to the binary action $\beta:(a,m)\to m$: send the ordered $a$-inputs to the first slot by their multiplication and the $m$-input to the second slot by its identity. The factorization map $(a^r,m)\to(a,m)$ belongs to $\mathrm{LM}_0$: its sole $m$-output has only its original $m$-input. The map $\beta$ itself is an active map of $\mathrm{LM}$, excluded from $\mathrm{LM}_0$, and represents an object of $J_m$. Composing this factorization map with $\beta$ gives the original ordered action. For $r=0$ the first component is the nullary unit operation, so the identity of $m$ also maps to $\beta$. Uniqueness follows from the prescribed input ordering. The slices are nerves of these ordinary categories, so these are terminal objects as infinity-categories as well.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.2.4.2: the two terminal active operations; their factorization written out, including r=0.

proof.text: The terminal comparison over $\mathrm{id}_a$ is the identity of $B$ and is $q$-cocartesian by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality]. Over $\beta$ the comparison is $(B,X)\to UL$ with underlying action composite $e=b_L\circ(B\otimes\lambda)$. By [lem-coef-module-operad-encoding], its cocartesian transport first produces $B\otimes X$; its remaining vertical comparison is exactly $e:B\otimes X\to UL$. The hypothesis says $e$ is an equivalence in the fiber. A fiberwise inverse for $e$ and its two inverse-triangle simplices are also inverse witnesses in the total category. Thus precomposition with $e$ on total mapping spaces has precomposition with that inverse as a homotopy inverse. Its base edge is an identity, so the square in [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] is a homotopy pullback; this vertical edge is $q$-cocartesian. Composition with the cocartesian transport is cocartesian by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality]. Consequently both terminal comparisons meet the hypotheses of the general terminal-active theorem.

source.place: Definition 4.2.4.1 and proof of Proposition 4.2.4.2: compare the binary-action transport with the displayed equivalence.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-coef-relative-operadic-terminal-active-mapping] with $\mathcal P=\mathrm{LM}_0$, $\mathcal Q=\mathcal O=\mathrm{LM}$, and the $A,F,\eta$ of Step 1. Both indexing operads are small, and Steps 2 and 3 check every color and the required cocartesian terminal edge. For the algebra $G$ corresponding to $(B,N)$, the resulting natural mapping-space equivalence becomes, by [lem-coef-module-operad-encoding],
$$\Psi:\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{LMod}(\mathcal M)}((B,L),(B,N))\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal V)}(B,B)\times\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal M}(X,UN).$$
It sends an algebra-changing module map $(h,f)$ to $(h,U(f)\lambda)$; in particular it commutes with projection to $S=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal V)}(B,B)$. The coordinate and parameter compatibility are part of the encoding, so the comparison retains the identity of $B$ and all higher homotopies.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.3.2 and proof of Proposition 4.2.4.2(2): relative free-algebra mapping property.

proof.text: Take the homotopy fiber of $\Psi$ over $\mathrm{id}_B\in S$. The projection $\Theta$ is a cartesian, hence inner, fibration by [lem-coef-module-operad-encoding]. Thus the map from its total module mapping space to $S$ is a Kan fibration by [lem-coef-infinity-inner-mapping-fiber]. Its strict fiber is the right-pinched mapping space in the degreewise fiber $\operatorname{LMod}_B(\mathcal M)$: a simplex has constant image $\mathrm{id}_B$ precisely when its defining pinched simplex lies over the constant object $B$. The product projection on the right of $\Psi$ is a Kan fibration: in a horn-lifting problem the $S$-coordinate is prescribed, and the other coordinate extends because $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal M}(X,UN)$ is Kan. By [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison], strict fibers compute both homotopy fibers. Apply [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance] to the cospans consisting of these projections and $\{\mathrm{id}_B\}\to S$, with maps $\Psi$, $\mathrm{id}_S$ and the identity of the point. The induced fiber map is an equivalence. Its left side is $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{LMod}_B(\mathcal M)}(L,N)$ and its right side is $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal M}(X,UN)$; by the formula in Step 4 it is exactly $f\mapsto U(f)\lambda$. Naturality in $N$ and coherent families of pairs follows by taking these fibers in the natural comparison of Step 4; no representing objects were chosen. This argument uses the given $L$ and the single equivalence $e$, and assumes no other colimits or presentability.

source.place: Corollary 4.2.4.6: fixed-algebra fiber of Proposition 4.2.4.2(2), with the fiber comparison written explicitly.

proof_origin.place: Independent expansion of the relative-operadic argument of Proposition 4.2.4.2 and Corollary 4.2.4.6, read online; Higher Algebra is not archived in literature/. The actual active factorizations and fixed-algebra homotopy-fiber comparison are written out here.
